title: The Hourglass Secret: Why the Sand's Weight Never Reaches the Bottom
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. It explains why sand in an hourglass flows at a steady rate no matter how full the upper bulb is, unlike water, whose flow slows as its level drops. It covers the Janssen effect, described by Hans Janssen in eighteen ninety-five from his corn silo measurements: friction against the walls carries the grains' weight, so the pressure at the bottom levels off once the column reaches a certain height. It also covers the Beverloo law of nineteen sixty-one, which ties the flow rate only to the width of the opening, and why silos burst because of the same physics.
